# Overview

`CALMeR` (Context-Aware Long-read MAPQ Rescuer) flags reads in long-read
transcriptome BAM files whose MAPQ is anomalously low *given* their
transcript context. It fits a Beta-Inflated (BEINF) regression model on
a sampled subset of reads, computes randomized quantile residuals on
the full table, and writes a filtered BAM plus a TSV of flagged reads.

The motivation: a uniform MAPQ threshold (e.g. `samtools view -q 30`)
disproportionately discards reads from highly multi-isoform genes,
GC-extreme transcripts, long transcripts, and reads on transcripts
that have a cross-gene paralog — not because the alignments are low
quality but because these transcript-level properties systematically
suppress MAPQ. CALMeR conditions on transcript context to distinguish
noise from biology.

The standard pipeline is one function per stage:

1. `make_paralog_table()` — run a minimap2 `asm20` self-alignment of the
   transcriptome FASTA and derive a per-transcript binary `has_paralog`
   flag (TRUE if the transcript has at least one cross-gene alignment
   passing `alen >= 50` and `query_cov >= 70%`). Run once per annotation.
2. `extract_features()` — read the BAM + GTF + transcriptome FASTA,
   build a per-read feature table (MAPQ, alignment length, transcript
   length, isoform count per gene, GC content, percent transcript
   covered, and the `has_paralog` flag joined from step 1).
3. `clean_features()` — apply the canonical preprocessing pipeline:
   primary-only filter, lump `n_isoforms` at 7, natural-log of
   `tx_length`, winsorize `pct_covered` at the 1st/99th percentiles
   (winsorize bounds attached as an attribute so the same bounds can
   be reused at scoring time).
4. `inspect_predictors()` — diagnostic plots of predictor distributions
   to inform downstream choices. Optional.
5. `fit_beinf()` — fit a single BEINF regression on a sampled training
   subset. Predictors split into three classes: `scaled_predictors`
   (z-scored, wrapped in `pb()`), `piecewise_predictors` (raw, two-piece
   linear basis with a knot), and `linear_predictors` (raw, plain linear).
6. `fit_beinf_suite()` — alternative to (5): fit a *suite* of up to 12
   variants for model comparison ({pb, linear} smoother × three
   interaction forms × with/without `has_paralog`). The suite is what
   `calmer_report()` ranks across to pick a primary model.
7. `score_reads()` — compute randomized quantile residuals for every
   read and flag those whose RQR falls in the lower tail. Accepts
   either a single `calmer_fit` or a `calmer_suite`.
8. `filter_bam()` — write a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) + a
   TSV of flagged reads with their feature values and residuals.
9. `calmer_report()` — render an HTML or PDF diagnostic report. When
   passed a `calmer_suite`, ranks all variants by AIC + BIC + Nagelkerke
   pseudo-R², picks the model with the smallest average rank, re-scores
   against the picked model, and runs the per-model diagnostic sections
   against the picked fit.

# End-to-end pipeline on bundled example data

CALMeR ships with a small example bundle (`calmer_example_data()`):
~2,000 reads from a real PCR cDNA long-read sample, a matching pruned
GTF and transcriptome FASTA, plus a precomputed `minimap2`
self-alignment PAF.

```{r pipeline}
library(CALMeR)
library(gamlss)   # so pb() resolves in user-supplied formulas

ex <- calmer_example_data()

# Compute the per-transcript paralog table (cached PAF in the bundle;
# in production this would invoke minimap2 once per annotation).
# The output is a 3-column table (transcript_id, gene_id, has_paralog).
paralog <- make_paralog_table(
    fasta    = ex$fasta,
    gtf      = ex$gtf,
    paf_path = ex$paf
)

features <- extract_features(ex$bam, ex$gtf, ex$fasta,
                             paralog_table = paralog)
clean    <- clean_features(features)

# A coarse 4-knot basis (inter = 4) on the three scaled predictors, plus
# the two-piece basis on n_isoforms and a linear has_paralog term. The
# default inter = 5 is fine for real data; we use a smaller basis here
# for the ~600-read bundled example to avoid knot-driven wiggles.
mu_rhs <- y ~ pb(tx_length_sc,   inter = 4) +
              pb(gc_content_sc,  inter = 4) +
              pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) +
              n_isoforms + I(pmax(n_isoforms - 5, 0)) +
              has_paralog
nu_rhs <-   ~ pb(tx_length_sc,   inter = 4) +
              pb(gc_content_sc,  inter = 4) +
              pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) +
              n_isoforms + I(pmax(n_isoforms - 5, 0)) +
              has_paralog

fit <- fit_beinf(
    clean, n = nrow(clean),
    scaled_predictors    = c("tx_length", "gc_content", "pct_covered"),
    piecewise_predictors = list(n_isoforms = 5),
    linear_predictors    = c("has_paralog"),
    formula              = mu_rhs,
    sigma_formula        = ~ 1,
    nu_formula           = nu_rhs,
    tau_formula          = nu_rhs
)

scored <- score_reads(clean, fit, filter_method = "mad", threshold = -3)
```

# Filtered outputs

`filter_bam()` writes a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) and a
gzipped TSV listing the flagged reads with their feature values and
residuals. Internal scaled-predictor columns (`*_sc`) are dropped from
the TSV — the file keeps the columns a user would actually inspect.

```{r filter}
filt <- filter_bam(
    bam     = ex$bam,
    scored  = scored,
    out_bam = tempfile(fileext = ".bam"),
    out_tsv = tempfile(fileext = ".tsv.gz")
)
filt$out_tsv
```

```{r filter-table, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
flagged_tbl <- readr::read_tsv(filt$out_tsv, show_col_types = FALSE)
cat('
<style>
.calmer-flagged-tbl { overflow-x: auto; margin: 1em 0; }
.calmer-flagged-tbl table { border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.9em; }
.calmer-flagged-tbl th, .calmer-flagged-tbl td {
    padding: 6px 14px;
    white-space: nowrap;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;
}
.calmer-flagged-tbl th { background: #f5f5f5; text-align: left; }
.calmer-flagged-tbl caption { caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-style: italic; padding: 4px 0; }
</style>
<div class="calmer-flagged-tbl">
')
print(knitr::kable(
    flagged_tbl, format = "html",
    caption = sprintf("Flagged reads (%d total, all %d columns shown — scroll horizontally).",
                      nrow(flagged_tbl), ncol(flagged_tbl))
))
cat("\n</div>\n")
```

# Diagnostic report (rendered inline)

The chunk below pulls in `inst/rmd/diagnostic_report.Rmd` as a child
document and renders it inline as part of this vignette. All sections
of the standalone report — predictor definitions, training summary,
model fit, model comparison (only if a suite was supplied), residual
diagnostics, partial effects, the coefficient forest plot, scoring
summary, and where flags landed — appear below.

```{r setup-report-params, include = FALSE}
# The report Rmd reads `params$fit`, `params$suite`, `params$scored`,
# `params$rank_table`, `params$picked_name`, and `params$sample_name`.
# When run as a child document, no params block is processed, so we
# define `params` in the parent environment and the child picks it up.
# For a single-fit vignette example, suite/rank_table/picked_name are
# NULL; the report's single-fit branches handle that.
params <- list(
    fit         = fit,
    suite       = NULL,
    scored      = scored,
    rank_table  = NULL,
    picked_name = NULL,
    sample_name = "vignette example (paralog-aware)"
)
```

```{r child = system.file("rmd", "diagnostic_report.Rmd", package = "CALMeR")}
```
